definitions.explanation: A ranking level in martial arts, board games like go or shogi, calligraphy, and other traditional Japanese disciplines. The dan system starts at 初段 (first dan) and goes up.

examples.japanese: {柔道|じゅうどう}の{段位|だんい}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: I hold a dan rank in judo.

examples.japanese: {段位|だんい}{審査|しんさ}を{受|う}けることにした。
examples.english: I decided to take the dan promotion exam.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{剣道|けんどう}{三段|さんだん}の{段位|だんい}を{取得|しゅとく}した。
examples.english: He earned a third-dan rank in kendo.

notes:
USAGE: The {段位|だんい} system (dan ranking) is used across many Japanese disciplines including martial arts ({柔道|じゅうどう}, {剣道|けんどう}, {空手|からて}), board games ({囲碁|いご}, {将棋|しょうぎ}), {書道|しょどう} (calligraphy), and {茶道|さどう} (tea ceremony).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {段位|だんい}を{取|と}る / {取得|しゅとく}する: to earn a dan rank
- {段位|だんい}{審査|しんさ}: dan examination/promotion test
- {段位|だんい}を{持|も}つ: to hold a dan rank
- {初段|しょだん}: first dan

Below the dan levels are {級|きゅう} (kyu) grades, which count downward (10th kyu being a beginner).
